what_it_does: This is an analog-to-digital converter (ADC)—a chip that translates continuous radio signals into digital numbers—designed for wide bandwidth (80 MHz) applications like wireless receivers. The challenge is that radio signals contain noise and out-of-band junk that must be filtered before conversion. This design embeds the filtering directly into the conversion process rather than requiring a separate filter chip, using a clever technique called progressive conversion that overlaps multiple processing stages to keep speed high while filtering is happening. The result is a very energy-efficient converter.
